text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Wednesday.
GERMANY - Bund futures continued to benefit from stronger Treasuries on Wednesday, raising expectations that the market has resumed its upward course of late last year.

The DTB Bund futures contract spent much of the day trading at strongly higher levels on Wednesday, but fell late in the afternoon to drift only a couple of basis points above the 101.24 close on Tuesday. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 101.31, up 0.11 from Tuesday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - UK gilt futures ended slightly higher after a session largely overshadowed by the monetary meeting between Chancellor Kenneth Clarke and Bank of England Governor Eddie George. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-29/32, up 5/32 from Tuesday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures climbed to the highest level since February 1994 as the euphoria that followed Tuesday's U.S. inflation data continued to buoy prices, flushing out some investors who had sold bonds previously. The March bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 130.22, up 0.18. from Tuesday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended lower, wiping out earlier gains which took the Btp Liffe March contract up to a new record high of 131.27, on a general wave of profit-taking, which also affected Milan stocks, and in line with easier U.S. Treasuries. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 130.63 down 0.02 from Tuesday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened higher on Wednesday, helped by a strong dollar, which continued its overnight rally in early dealings, touching 1.60 marks, its highest level since July 1994, and holding above 117 yen, near a fresh 46-month high. The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 111-5/32, down 8/32 from Tuesday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.8 percent.
JAPAN - The Tokyo market was closed Wednesday for a national holiday. Trade will resume on Thursday.
On Tuesday, the key March Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended the session slightly higher in dealer-led trade. The March closed up 0.06 at 125.73.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - As anticipated, New York City launched its first Eurobond in an active session on Wednesday.
The $300 million five-year FRN will be priced in the afternoon session to yield between 28 and 32 basis points over three-month LIBOR.
